pra.name: Pre-Prophethood
pra.desc: Arabia before prophethood: the Ka'bah, Quraysh, Year of the Elephant, and key figures around the Prophet's birth.

makkah.name: Mecca Period
makkah.desc: First revelation, secret and public preaching, Quraysh persecution, and migration to Abyssinia.

madinah.name: Medina Period
madinah.desc: The Hijrah and Medina state, battles from Badr to Khandaq, Hudaybiyyah, Fathu Makkah, and the Prophet's passing.

khulafaur.name: Khulafaur Rasyidin
khulafaur.desc: The first four caliphs—Abu Bakar, Umar, Utsman, and Ali—expanding across Syria, Persia, and Egypt.

umayyah.name: Umayyad Caliphate
umayyah.desc: Governance from Damascus, expansion into Andalusia and Sindh, and the birth of monumental Islamic architecture.

abbasiyah.name: Abbasid Golden Age
abbasiyah.desc: Baghdad as a global center of scholarship, translation, and science alongside Cordoba and Fatimid Cairo.

seljuk.name: Seljuk, Crusades & Mongols
seljuk.desc: Seljuk rise, the Crusades, Salahuddin al-Ayyubi, and the Mongol sack of Baghdad.

mamluk.name: Mamluk & Post-Mongol
mamluk.desc: Mamluks halting the Mongols at Ain Jalut, Ottoman rise, fall of Granada, and Nusantara sultanates.

imperium.name: Three Gunpowder Empires
imperium.desc: Ottoman, Safavid, and Mughal empires at their peak while Nusantara sultanates confronted the VOC.

kolonial.name: Colonialism & Reform
kolonial.desc: The Muslim world facing European colonialism, reformist movements, and the abolition of the caliphate.

modern.name: Modern Era
modern.desc: Nation-states, independence movements, modern Islamic organizations, and contemporary geopolitical shifts.

makkah.name: Mecca
makkah.subtitle: Birthplace of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ
makkah.description: Commercial and spiritual hub of the Arabian Peninsula where the Ka'bah stands under Quraysh guardianship.

yatsrib.name: Yathrib (Medina)
yatsrib.subtitle: Oasis north of Mecca
yatsrib.description: Fertile oasis inhabited by Aws, Khazraj, and Jewish tribes; became the destination of the Hijrah in 622 CE.

syam.name: Syam (Levant)
syam.subtitle: Quraysh caravan destination
syam.description: Northern trade route of Quraysh caravans where young Muhammad met monk Bahira in Busra.

palestina.name: Palestine
palestina.subtitle: Land of Baitul Maqdis
palestina.description: Region housing Masjid al-Aqsa, the first Qibla of Muslims before Mecca.

iraq.name: Iraq (Ancient)
iraq.subtitle: Under Sassanid Persian sphere
iraq.description: Region under the Sassanid Empire before the campaigns of Qadisiyyah and the founding of Kufah.

yaman.name: Yemen
yaman.subtitle: Domain of Abrahah
yaman.description: Southern Arabian territory governed by Abrahah on behalf of the Aksumite Kingdom.

gajah.name: Route of the Elephant Army
gajah.subtitle: Yemen toward Mecca, c. 570 CE
gajah.description: Campaign route of Abrahah's army marching toward Mecca before perishing outside the sanctuary.

hira.name: Cave of Hira
hira.subtitle: Jabal al-Nour, near Mecca
hira.description: Mountain cave where Prophet Muhammad ﷺ retreated in contemplation and received the first revelation in 610 CE.

makkah-k.name: Mecca
makkah-k.subtitle: Sanctuary of the Ka'bah
makkah-k.description: Opened nearly without bloodshed during Fathu Makkah (8 AH / 630 CE), remaining the center of Hajj.

madinah-k.name: Medina
madinah-k.subtitle: First capital of the Islamic state
madinah-k.description: Seat of governance from the Hijrah through the era of Utsman; home to the Prophet's Mosque.

badar.name: Badr
badar.subtitle: Valley of the first major battle
badar.description: Site of the Battle of Badr (17 Ramadan 2 AH / 624 CE), where 313 Muslims defeated a larger Quraysh force.

khaibar.name: Khaybar
khaibar.subtitle: Fortified oasis north of Medina
khaibar.description: Walled agricultural oasis captured in 7 AH / 628 CE.

tabuk.name: Tabuk
tabuk.subtitle: The Prophet's final campaign
tabuk.description: Northern frontier expedition in 9 AH / 630 CE facing Byzantine mobilization.

yamamah.name: Yamamah
yamamah.subtitle: Battlefield of the Riddah Wars
yamamah.description: Interior Najd plain where Khalid bin Walid defeated Musaylimah in 12 AH / 633 CE.

damaskus.name: Damascus
damaskus.subtitle: Capital of Syam
damaskus.description: Ancient Levantine city taken in 14 AH / 635 CE under Khalid bin Walid and Abu Ubaidah.

yarmuk.name: Yarmuk
yarmuk.subtitle: Decisive battle for Syam
yarmuk.description: Site of the 636 CE victory over Byzantine forces that opened all of Greater Syria.

baitulmaqdis.name: Baitul Maqdis
baitulmaqdis.subtitle: Jerusalem, the first Qibla
baitulmaqdis.description: Surrendered peacefully to Caliph Umar bin Khattab in 16 AH / 637 CE under a treaty protecting lives and worship.

hims.name: Homs (Hims)
hims.subtitle: Northern Syrian city
hims.description: Strategic Syrian city conquered after Yarmuk; resting place of Khalid bin Walid.

konstantinopel.name: Constantinople
konstantinopel.subtitle: Byzantine imperial capital
konstantinopel.description: Fortified capital on the Bosphorus besieged multiple times before falling in 1453 CE.

iskandariyah.name: Alexandria
iskandariyah.subtitle: Major Mediterranean port of Egypt
iskandariyah.description: Byzantine port city captured by Amr bin Ash in 21 AH / 642 CE.

fustat.name: Fustat
fustat.subtitle: First Islamic capital in Egypt
fustat.description: Garrison city founded by Amr bin Ash around 20 AH with the first mosque in Africa.

barqah.name: Barqah (Cyrenaica)
barqah.subtitle: Eastern Libya gateway
barqah.description: Region opened by Amr bin Ash around 22 AH / 643 CE on the road to North Africa.

kufah.name: Kufah & Qadisiyyah
kufah.subtitle: Iraqi garrison hub
kufah.description: Site of the 636 CE victory over Sassanid Persia, followed by Sa'ad bin Abi Waqqash founding Kufah.

madain.name: Al-Mada'in (Ctesiphon)
madain.subtitle: Sassanid imperial capital
madain.description: Persian capital captured in 16 AH / 637 CE following the Battle of Qadisiyyah.

basrah.name: Basra
basrah.subtitle: Southern Iraq garrison city
basrah.description: Port and military base founded around 14 AH; nearby site of the Battle of the Camel in 36 AH.

nahawand.name: Nahawand
nahawand.subtitle: Victory of Victories
nahawand.description: Decisive 21 AH / 642 CE battle breaking organized Sassanid resistance on the Iranian plateau.

merv.name: Merv
merv.subtitle: Eastern frontier of Khorasan
merv.description: Oasis city near which the last Sassanid ruler Yazdegerd III died in 31 AH / 651 CE.

habasyah.name: Abyssinia (Aksum)
habasyah.subtitle: First sanctuary of migration
habasyah.description: Christian kingdom in modern Ethiopia where King Negus protected early Muslim refugees in 615 CE.

570-tahun-gajah.title: Year of the Elephant
570-tahun-gajah.summary: Abrahah marched from Yemen with war elephants to destroy the Ka'bah, but his army perished before reaching Mecca (Surah Al-Fil).

570-kelahiran-nabi.title: Birth of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ
570-kelahiran-nabi.summary: Born in Mecca to Aminah binti Wahb; his father Abdullah had passed away earlier, leaving grandfather Abdul Muthalib as guardian.

572-disusui-siti-halimah.title: Fostering with Halimah as-Sa'diyah
572-disusui-siti-halimah.summary: Following Quraysh custom, infant Muhammad was raised in the desert air of Bani Sa'd by Halimah as-Sa'diyah.

576-yatim-piatu.title: Orphaned in Childhood
576-yatim-piatu.summary: Aminah passed away returning from Yathrib; two years later Abdul Muthalib died, and Abu Thalib assumed guardianship.

582-bertemu-bahira.title: Meeting Monk Bahira
582-bertemu-bahira.summary: During a trade caravan to Syam with Abu Thalib, the Christian monk Bahira in Busra recognized signs of prophethood.

595-menikah-dengan-khadijah.title: Marriage to Khadijah
595-menikah-dengan-khadijah.summary: Known across Mecca as Al-Amin after leading her trade caravan to Syam, Muhammad ﷺ married Khadijah binti Khuwailid.

605-peletakan-hajar-aswad.title: Placing the Black Stone
605-peletakan-hajar-aswad.summary: When Quraysh clans disputed who would set the Black Stone during Ka'bah renovations, Muhammad ﷺ had all clan chiefs lift it together on a cloak.

610-wahyu-pertama.title: The First Revelation
610-wahyu-pertama.summary: In the Cave of Hira, Angel Jibril delivered the opening verses of Surah Al-'Alaq ('Iqra'), marking the dawn of prophethood.

613-dakwah-terang-terangan.title: Public Preaching Begins
613-dakwah-terang-terangan.summary: After three years of quiet invitation, the Prophet ﷺ proclaimed Islam openly in Mecca amid intensifying Quraysh opposition.

615-hijrah-ke-habasyah.title: Migration to Abyssinia
615-hijrah-ke-habasyah.summary: Early Muslims fled Quraysh persecution to Aksum, where King Negus granted them safe refuge.

619-pemboikotan-dan-tahun-duka-cita.title: Boycott & Year of Sorrow
619-pemboikotan-dan-tahun-duka-cita.summary: Following a three-year clan boycott in Shi'b Abi Thalib, both Abu Thalib and Khadijah passed away in 619 CE.

621-isra-dan-miraj.title: Isra' and Mi'raj
621-isra-dan-miraj.summary: The miraculous night journey from Mecca to Masjid al-Aqsa and ascension through the heavens, establishing the five daily prayers.

622-hijrah-ke-madinah.title: The Hijrah to Medina
622-hijrah-ke-madinah.summary: After the Pledges of Aqabah, the Prophet ﷺ migrated with Abu Bakar to Yathrib (Medina), inaugurating the Hijri calendar.

624-perang-badar.title: Battle of Badr
624-perang-badar.summary: The first major battle of Islam: 313 Muslims defeated a much larger Quraysh army, and Abu Jahal was killed here, marking a decisive turning point.

625-perang-uhud.title: Battle of Uhud
625-perang-uhud.summary: Fought at Mount Uhud; archers leaving their post allowed Khalid bin Walid's cavalry to flank, and Hamzah fell in battle.

627-perang-khandaq.title: Battle of the Trench (Khandaq)
627-perang-khandaq.summary: Coalition forces besieged Medina; adopting Salman al-Farisi's trench defense preserved the city.

628-perjanjian-hudaibiyah.title: Treaty of Hudaybiyyah
628-perjanjian-hudaibiyah.summary: A ten-year truce negotiated outside Mecca that opened peaceful outreach across Arabia.

630-fathu-makkah.title: Fathu Makkah (Opening of Mecca)
630-fathu-makkah.summary: Prophet Muhammad ﷺ entered Mecca with 10,000 troops virtually unopposed, granting general amnesty and clearing the Ka'bah.

632-haji-wada-dan-wafatnya-nabi.title: Farewell Pilgrimage & Passing of the Prophet
632-haji-wada-dan-wafatnya-nabi.summary: After delivering the Farewell Sermon at Arafah, Prophet Muhammad ﷺ passed away in Medina on 12 Rabi'ul Awwal 11 AH.

632-abu-bakar-menjadi-khalifah.title: Abu Bakar Elected Caliph
632-abu-bakar-menjadi-khalifah.summary: Abu Bakar ash-Shiddiq stabilized Arabia during the Riddah Wars, culminating against Musaylimah at Yamamah.

636-penaklukan-syam-dan-yarmuk.title: Conquest of Syam & Battle of Yarmuk
636-penaklukan-syam-dan-yarmuk.summary: Muslim forces captured Damascus and broke Byzantine military dominance in the Levant at the Yarmuk River.

636-qadisiyyah-dan-madain.title: Battle of Qadisiyyah & Al-Mada'in
636-qadisiyyah-dan-madain.summary: Sa'ad bin Abi Waqqash defeated Sassanid forces at Qadisiyyah and captured Ctesiphon, founding Kufah and Basra.

637-penyerahan-baitul-maqdis.title: Surrender of Baitul Maqdis (Jerusalem)
637-penyerahan-baitul-maqdis.summary: Residents of Jerusalem surrendered to Caliph Umar bin Khattab under a covenant guaranteeing protection of lives and churches.

639-penaklukan-mesir.title: Conquest of Egypt
639-penaklukan-mesir.summary: Amr bin Ash entered Egypt, captured Babylon Fortress and Alexandria, and founded Fustat.

644-wafatnya-umar-utsman-menjadi-khalifa.title: Death of Umar & Caliphate of Utsman
644-wafatnya-umar-utsman-menjadi-khalifa.summary: Following Umar's assassination at dawn prayer, a six-member council selected Utsman bin Affan as the third caliph.

650-mushaf-utsmani.title: Compilation of the Uthmani Mushaf
650-mushaf-utsmani.summary: Utsman standardized the written Quranic codex and dispatched copies to major provinces as borders reached Armenia and Khorasan.

656-wafatnya-utsman-ali-menjadi-khalifah.title: Death of Utsman & Caliphate of Ali
656-wafatnya-utsman-ali-menjadi-khalifah.summary: Amid political turmoil in Medina, Utsman was slain and Ali bin Abi Thalib was pledged allegiance, later shifting the seat to Kufah.

656-perang-jamal-dan-shiffin.title: Battles of the Camel & Siffin
656-perang-jamal-dan-shiffin.summary: Disputes over Utsman's assassination sparked internal conflicts near Basra and at Siffin against Mu'awiyah.

661-wafatnya-ali.title: Martyrdom of Ali bin Abi Thalib
661-wafatnya-ali.summary: Ali was fatally struck in Kufah by Ibn Muljam, bringing the Khulafaur Rasyidin era to a close.

661-daulah-umayyah-berdiri.title: Founding of the Umayyad Caliphate
661-daulah-umayyah-berdiri.summary: After Hasan bin Ali abdicated to preserve unity ('Aam al-Jama'ah), Mu'awiyah established Umayyad rule in Damascus.

680-peristiwa-karbala.title: Tragedy of Karbala
680-peristiwa-karbala.summary: Husain bin Ali and his companions fell at Karbala on 10 Muharram 61 AH against Yazid's forces.

691-kubah-shakhrah-dibangun-di-yerusalem.title: Completion of the Dome of the Rock
691-kubah-shakhrah-dibangun-di-yerusalem.summary: Caliph Abdul Malik bin Marwan built Qubbat ash-Shakhrah in Jerusalem, the oldest surviving monumental Islamic sanctuary.

706-masjid-agung-umawi-damaskus.title: Great Mosque of Damascus
706-masjid-agung-umawi-damaskus.summary: Under Caliph Al-Walid I, the Umayyad Mosque of Damascus set a benchmark for early Islamic architecture.

711-penaklukan-andalusia.title: Crossing to Al-Andalus (Iberia)
711-penaklukan-andalusia.summary: Thariq bin Ziyad crossed Gibraltar and defeated King Roderic at Guadalete, inaugurating Islamic Iberia.

712-islam-masuk-ke-sindh.title: Arrival in Sindh
712-islam-masuk-ke-sindh.summary: Muhammad bin Qasim entered the Indus Valley (modern Pakistan), establishing early Islamic presence in South Asia.

717-pengepungan-konstantinopel-kedua.title: Second Siege of Constantinople
717-pengepungan-konstantinopel-kedua.summary: Umayyad land and naval forces under Maslamah besieged Constantinople for nearly a year before withdrawing.

732-pertempuran-tours-poitiers.title: Battle of Tours (Poitiers)
732-pertempuran-tours-poitiers.summary: Andalusian forces under Abdurrahman al-Ghafiqi were halted by Charles Martel's Frankish army in central France.

750-revolusi-abbasiyah.title: The Abbasid Revolution
750-revolusi-abbasiyah.summary: Abbasid forces defeated the Umayyads at the Battle of the Zab, proclaiming Abu al-Abbas as-Saffah caliph.

751-pertempuran-talas.title: Battle of Talas
751-pertempuran-talas.summary: Abbasid troops defeated Tang Dynasty forces near the Talas River, accelerating the spread of papermaking westward.

756-emirat-cordoba-berdiri.title: Emirate of Cordoba Founded
756-emirat-cordoba-berdiri.summary: Surviving Umayyad prince Abdurrahman ad-Dakhil established an independent emirate centered in Cordoba.

762-baghdad-didirikan.title: Founding of Baghdad
762-baghdad-didirikan.summary: Caliph Al-Mansur built the Round City of Baghdad on the Tigris, soon becoming a global center of scholarship.

786-masa-harun-ar-rasyid.title: Reign of Harun ar-Rasyid
786-masa-harun-ar-rasyid.summary: Height of Abbasid prosperity, diplomacy, and patronage of scholars and translators in Baghdad.

820-al-khawarizmi-dan-ilmu-aljabar.title: Al-Khawarizmi & Algebra
820-al-khawarizmi-dan-ilmu-aljabar.summary: Muhammad bin Musa al-Khawarizmi authored his foundational treatise on algebra in Baghdad; his Latinized name gave us 'algorithm'.

830-baitul-hikmah-di-baghdad.title: Bayt al-Hikmah (House of Wisdom)
830-baitul-hikmah-di-baghdad.summary: Under Al-Ma'mun, Baghdad's academy translated and advanced Greek, Persian, and Indian scientific works.

859-al-qarawiyyin-didirikan-di-fez.title: Founding of Al-Qarawiyyin in Fez
859-al-qarawiyyin-didirikan-di-fez.summary: Fatima al-Fihri founded Al-Qarawiyyin, recognized as one of the oldest continuously operating universities.

909-dinasti-fatimiyah-berdiri.title: Rise of the Fatimid Caliphate
909-dinasti-fatimiyah-berdiri.summary: The Fatimid dynasty took power in Ifriqiya (Tunisia) before expanding into Egypt.

929-khilafah-cordoba-diproklamasikan.title: Caliphate of Cordoba Proclaimed
929-khilafah-cordoba-diproklamasikan.summary: Abdurrahman III proclaimed the Caliphate of Cordoba, ushering in Andalusian cultural splendor.

969-kairo-didirikan.title: Founding of Cairo
969-kairo-didirikan.summary: The Fatimids founded Al-Qahirah (Cairo) as their new imperial capital on the Nile.

970-al-azhar-didirikan.title: Founding of Al-Azhar
970-al-azhar-didirikan.summary: Al-Azhar Mosque was built in Cairo and evolved into one of the foremost centers of Islamic learning.

1011-ibnu-al-haitham-dan-ilmu-optik.title: Ibn al-Haytham & Optics
1011-ibnu-al-haitham-dan-ilmu-optik.summary: In Cairo, Ibn al-Haytham wrote Kitab al-Manazir (Book of Optics), pioneering experimental scientific method.

1037-wafatnya-ibnu-sina.title: Passing of Ibn Sina (Avicenna)
1037-wafatnya-ibnu-sina.summary: Physician and philosopher Ibn Sina, author of The Canon of Medicine, passed away in Hamadan.

1055-seljuk-memasuki-baghdad.title: Seljuks Enter Baghdad
1055-seljuk-memasuki-baghdad.summary: Tughril Beg entered Baghdad, becoming protector of the Abbasid caliphate.

1071-pertempuran-manzikert.title: Battle of Manzikert
1071-pertempuran-manzikert.summary: Seljuk Sultan Alp Arslan defeated Byzantine Emperor Romanos IV, opening Anatolia to Turkic settlement.

1096-perang-salib-pertama.title: The First Crusade
1096-perang-salib-pertama.summary: European Crusader armies marched east, establishing Crusader states along the Levantine coast.

1099-yerusalem-jatuh-ke-tangan-pasukan-s.title: Crusader Capture of Jerusalem
1099-yerusalem-jatuh-ke-tangan-pasukan-s.summary: Crusader forces breached Jerusalem following a prolonged siege.

1111-wafatnya-al-ghazali.title: Passing of Imam al-Ghazali
1111-wafatnya-al-ghazali.summary: Scholar and theologian Abu Hamid al-Ghazali, author of Ihya' Ulumiddin, passed away in Tus.

1187-salahuddin-al-ayyubi-merebut-yerusa.title: Salahuddin Recaptures Jerusalem
1187-salahuddin-al-ayyubi-merebut-yerusa.summary: Following victory at Hattin, Salahuddin al-Ayyubi reclaimed Jerusalem under terms guaranteeing civilian safety.

1192-perjanjian-ramla.title: Treaty of Ramla
1192-perjanjian-ramla.summary: Salahuddin and Richard the Lionheart agreed to a truce ending the Third Crusade and allowing Christian pilgrims.

1198-wafatnya-ibnu-rusyd.title: Passing of Ibn Rushd (Averroes)
1198-wafatnya-ibnu-rusyd.summary: Andalusian jurist and philosopher Ibn Rushd passed away in Marrakesh.

1219-invasi-mongol-ke-khwarezmia.title: Mongol Invasion of Khwarazmia
1219-invasi-mongol-ke-khwarezmia.summary: Genghis Khan's armies devastated Central Asian cities including Bukhara, Samarkand, and Merv.

1258-jatuhnya-baghdad.title: Fall of Baghdad
1258-jatuhnya-baghdad.summary: Hulagu Khan's Mongol forces sacked Baghdad, ending the Abbasid Caliphate in Iraq.

1260-pertempuran-ain-jalut.title: Battle of Ain Jalut
1260-pertempuran-ain-jalut.summary: Mamluk forces led by Qutuz and Baybars defeated the Mongols in Palestine, halting their westward advance.

1297-wafatnya-sultan-malik-as-saleh-samu.title: Tombstone of Sultan Malik as-Saleh, Samudra Pasai
1297-wafatnya-sultan-malik-as-saleh-samu.summary: Dated 696 AH (1297 CE) in Aceh, providing the earliest epigraphic evidence of a Muslim kingdom in Nusantara.

1299-awal-berdirinya-kesultanan-utsmani.title: Founding of the Ottoman Beylik
1299-awal-berdirinya-kesultanan-utsmani.summary: Osman I established a frontier principality in northwestern Anatolia that grew into the Ottoman Empire.

1325-ibnu-battuta-memulai-pengembaraanny.title: Ibn Battuta Begins His Travels
1325-ibnu-battuta-memulai-pengembaraanny.summary: Departing Tangier for Hajj, Ibn Battuta journeyed across Africa, Asia, and Europe for nearly thirty years.

1345-ibnu-battuta-singgah-di-samudra-pas.title: Ibn Battuta Visits Samudra Pasai
1345-ibnu-battuta-singgah-di-samudra-pas.summary: En route to China, Ibn Battuta visited Samudra Pasai in Sumatra and recorded life at its court.

1370-timur-lenk-berkuasa.title: Rise of Timur (Tamerlane)
1370-timur-lenk-berkuasa.summary: Making Samarkand his capital, Timur launched sweeping campaigns across Central Asia, Persia, and Anatolia.

1377-ibnu-khaldun-menulis-muqaddimah.title: Ibn Khaldun Writes the Muqaddimah
1377-ibnu-khaldun-menulis-muqaddimah.summary: Ibn Khaldun completed the Muqaddimah, pioneering historiography, sociology, and economic theory.

1414-malaka-menjadi-pusat-dagang-dan-isl.title: Malacca as Trade & Islamic Hub
1414-malaka-menjadi-pusat-dagang-dan-isl.summary: By the early 15th century, Malacca emerged as Southeast Asia's premier maritime port and center of Islamic diffusion.

1419-wafatnya-maulana-malik-ibrahim.title: Passing of Maulana Malik Ibrahim
1419-wafatnya-maulana-malik-ibrahim.summary: Early Islamic preacher in Java and revered member of the Walisongo, buried in Gresik.

1453-penaklukan-konstantinopel.title: Conquest of Constantinople
1453-penaklukan-konstantinopel.summary: Ottoman Sultan Mehmed II captured Constantinople, ending the Byzantine Empire.

1478-kesultanan-demak-berdiri.title: Founding of the Demak Sultanate
1478-kesultanan-demak-berdiri.summary: Demak emerged as the first Islamic sultanate on Java under Raden Patah in the late 15th century.

1492-jatuhnya-granada.title: Fall of Granada
1492-jatuhnya-granada.summary: The Emirate of Granada, last Muslim polity in Iberia, surrendered to Castile and Aragon.

1501-dinasti-safawiyah-berdiri.title: Rise of the Safavid Dynasty
1501-dinasti-safawiyah-berdiri.summary: Shah Ismail I took Tabriz and established Twelver Shi'ism as the state creed of Persia.

1511-portugis-merebut-malaka.title: Portuguese Capture of Malacca
1511-portugis-merebut-malaka.summary: Portuguese forces seized Malacca, shifting regional Muslim trade toward Aceh, Banten, and Makassar.

1511-kesultanan-aceh-darussalam-berdiri.title: Rise of Aceh Darussalam
1511-kesultanan-aceh-darussalam-berdiri.summary: Aceh consolidated as a major maritime Islamic sultanate at the northern tip of Sumatra.

1517-utsmani-menaklukkan-mesir.title: Ottoman Conquest of Egypt
1517-utsmani-menaklukkan-mesir.summary: Sultan Selim I defeated the Mamluks, incorporating Egypt and the Hijaz under Ottoman protection.

1520-masa-sulaiman-al-qanuni.title: Reign of Suleiman the Magnificent
1520-masa-sulaiman-al-qanuni.summary: Ottoman zenith marked by legal codification, Mimar Sinan's architecture, and territorial peak.

1526-pertempuran-panipat-dan-awal-mughal.title: Battle of Panipat & Mughal Founding
1526-pertempuran-panipat-dan-awal-mughal.summary: Babur defeated the Delhi Sultanate at Panipat, establishing the Mughal Empire in India.

1527-fatahillah-merebut-sunda-kelapa.title: Fatahillah Captures Sunda Kelapa
1527-fatahillah-merebut-sunda-kelapa.summary: Joint Banten and Demak forces under Fatahillah took Sunda Kelapa, renaming it Jayakarta.

1529-pengepungan-wina-pertama.title: First Siege of Vienna
1529-pengepungan-wina-pertama.summary: Suleiman's forces besieged Vienna before retreating, marking the farthest Ottoman push of that era.

1556-masa-akbar-agung.title: Reign of Emperor Akbar
1556-masa-akbar-agung.summary: Akbar expanded Mughal rule across northern India while pursuing religious pluralism and administrative reform.

1571-pertempuran-lepanto.title: Battle of Lepanto
1571-pertempuran-lepanto.summary: A Holy League fleet defeated the Ottoman navy in the Gulf of Patras, though the Ottomans rapidly rebuilt.

1588-masa-syah-abbas-i.title: Reign of Shah Abbas I
1588-masa-syah-abbas-i.summary: Shah Abbas moved the Safavid capital to Isfahan, turning it into a jewel of Persian art and architecture.

1613-sultan-agung-dari-mataram.title: Sultan Agung of Mataram
1613-sultan-agung-dari-mataram.summary: Sultan Agung brought Islamic Mataram to its height on Java, synthesizing Javanese and Islamic statecraft.

1619-voc-mendirikan-batavia.title: VOC Establishes Batavia

Abdul Muthalib.meta:
Birth name: Syaibah al-Hamd
Era/Setting: Mecca, late 6th century CE
Abdul Muthalib.body:
Lineage & Early Life

Shaybah al-Hamd (Abdul Muthalib bin Hashim) was the supreme chieftain of Quraysh and the beloved grandfather and guardian of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ. Known for his generosity, towering stature, and wisdom, he was dubbed Sayyid al-Bat-ha (Chieftain of the Valley of Mecca).

Key Events & Historical Role

1. Re-excavation of the Well of Zamzam

  • Divine Inspiration: Guided by visionary dreams, Abdul Muthalib successfully rediscovered and re-excavated the blessed well of Zamzam, which had been buried for generations by the Jurhum tribe, securing precious water for pilgrims.

2. Confronting Abrahah (Year of the Elephant)

  • Majestic Dignity: When Abrahah invaded Mecca to raze the Ka'bah, Abdul Muthalib confronted him with serene resolve, declaring: "I am the owner of the camels, and the House has a Lord who will protect it." He gathered Quraysh in supplication atop Mount Abu Qubays until divine aid destroyed the invaders.

3. Loving Care for Young Muhammad

  • Guardian & Champion: Upon the passing of Aminah, he took the orphan Muhammad into his intimate home, honoring him above his own sons and seating him beside himself upon his royal rug in the shade of the Ka'bah.

Passing & Historical Legacy

Abdul Muthalib passed away in Mecca when young Muhammad was eight years old. On his deathbed, he entrusted Muhammad's guardianship to his noble son Abu Talib, leaving a legacy of integrity and righteous pre-Islamic leadership.

Abrahah.meta:
Viceroy of Yemen for the Kingdom of Aksum
Era/Setting: Yemen and Mecca, c. 570 CE
Abrahah.body:
Background & Rule in Yemen

Abrahah al-Ashram was the military viceroy who ruled Yemen under the authority of the Christian Kingdom of Aksum (Abyssinia) in the 6th century CE. Driven by ambition to divert Arabian pilgrimage and trade toward Yemen, he constructed a magnificent cathedral in Sana'a known as Al-Qullays.

Key Events & Historical Role

1. Construction of Al-Qullays Cathedral

  • Imperial Ambition: Built using imported marble, gilded mosaics, and precious timbers with the explicit geopolitical aim of replacing Mecca as the primary pilgrimage center of Arabia.

2. The Expedition of the Elephant (570 CE)

  • March on the Ka'bah: Enraged after a tribesman defiled Al-Qullays, Abrahah mobilized a formidable army equipped with war elephants (led by the colossal elephant Mahmud) intending to demolish the Ka'bah entirely.

  • Encounter with Abdul Muthalib: Seizing two hundred camels belonging to the chieftain Abdul Muthalib, Abrahah granted him an audience. When Abdul Muthalib demanded his camels back, stating "I am the lord of the camels, and the House has a Lord who will defend it," Abrahah marveled at his dignity.

  • Miraculous Destruction at Wadi Muhassir: Upon reaching the borders of the Haram, the lead elephant knelt and refused to advance toward Mecca. Flocks of birds (Ababil) pelted the army with stones of baked clay, decimating the invading force as commemorated in Surah Al-Fil.

Death & Historical Impact

Abrahah retreated wounded and dismembered to Sana'a where he perished shortly thereafter. His failed expedition cemented the sanctity of the Ka'bah across Arabia and marked 570 CE as the Year of the Elephant, the monumental year in which Prophet Muhammad ﷺ was born.

Bahira.meta:
Monk in Busra, Syam
Era/Setting: Busra (Syria), c. 582 CE
Bahira.body:
Lineage & Early Life

Monk Bahira (Buhayra) was a revered Christian monk and ascetic who resided in his secluded monastery in the environs of Busra, within the Levant (modern-day southern Syria). He was widely recognized as the most profoundly knowledgeable and erudite scholar of Christian scripture of his generation. His deep familiarity with ancient holy texts—including the Gospel and the Torah—derived from authoritative scriptural manuscripts inherited through successive generations of monastic scholars.

Key Events & Historical Role

1. Witnessing Signs of Prophethood in Nature

  • The Shading Cloud and Bowing Trees: When the Quraysh merchant caravan bearing young Muhammad (aged approximately nine to twelve) paused in Busra, Bahira beheld an extraordinary omen from his monastery. He observed a solitary cloud constantly shielding young Muhammad from the scorching desert sun, while branches of the tree beneath which he sat lowered to envelop him in comforting shade.

2. Hosting a Special Feast for the Quraysh Caravan

  • The Feast Initiative: Although Quraysh merchants had regularly traversed this trade route for decades without formal reception, Bahira prepared an abundant feast and extended a personal invitation to every member of the convoy—young and old, enslaved and freeborn alike.

  • Seeking the Prophet's Presence: As the merchants gathered to dine, Bahira surveyed their faces and realized the sought-after youth was not among them, having been left to guard the caravan baggage beneath a tree. Bahira insisted the child be summoned and honored at the meal.

3. Examining the Seal of Prophethood (Khatamun Nubuwwah)

  • Inquiry and Character Discernment: Bahira engaged young Muhammad in gentle conversation, inquiring about his sleep, waking life, and personal conduct. When Bahira swore by Al-Lat and Al-Uzza, young Muhammad firmly voiced his detestation of the idols, prompting Bahira to invoke only the name of God.

  • Observing the Prophetic Seal: Bahira examined the youth's upper back between the shoulder blades and identified the Khatam an-Nubuwwah (Seal of Prophethood), matching precisely the physical description recorded in ancient prophetic manuscripts.

4. Warning and Counsel to Abu Talib

  • Lineage Confirmation: Bahira asked Abu Talib about his kinship to the boy. When Abu Talib explained that he was his nephew whose father had passed away before his birth, Bahira verified that this orphan status strictly matched the prophecies.

  • Counsel to Return to Mecca: Bahira urged Abu Talib to swiftly escort Muhammad back to Mecca and protect him with utmost vigilance against hostile factions who might recognize the prophetic signs and conspire against him. Hearing this grave counsel, Abu Talib arranged his safe return to Mecca.

5. Protecting Muhammad from Hostile People of the Book

  • Warding Off Danger: When other scholars (such as Zurayr, Tamam, and Daris) recognized the portents of prophethood and conspired to inflict harm, Bahira confronted and counseled them with the divine decrees in the scriptures until they repented and withdrew their hostility.

Passing

No definitive historical record records the exact year of Monk Bahira's passing in primary biographical works (sirah nabawiyyah). He remains honored in Islamic history as an early monotheist scholar who recognized and affirmed the impending divine mission of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ during his youth.

Khadijah.meta:
Title: Ummul Mukminin, At-Thahirah
Era/Setting: Mecca, 6th–7th century CE
Khadijah.body:
Lineage & Early Life

Sayyidah Khadijah binti Khuwaylid bin Asad belonged to the noble Qurayshi clan of Banu Asad. Known prior to Islam as At-Tahirah (The Pure One) and Sayyidatu Quraysh, she was an eminent and prosperous merchant whose noble character, intelligence, and business acumen commanded universal respect throughout Arabia.

Key Events & Historical Role

1. Trade Partnership & Marriage

  • Hiring Al-Amin: Recognizing his flawless honesty and truthfulness, Khadijah entrusted young Muhammad with her Syrian trade caravan under the accompaniment of her servant Maysarah, yielding unprecedented profit and ethical praise.

  • The Blessed Marriage: Impressed by his peerless virtues, Khadijah proposed marriage to Muhammad ﷺ, entering into a twenty-five-year sacred union filled with steadfast love, loyalty, and companionship.

2. The First to Believe & Steadfast Supporter

  • Comforting the Prophet: When the first revelation descended upon Muhammad ﷺ in Cave Hira trembling, she enveloped him with comfort and uttered the historic words: "By Allah, Allah will never disgrace you; you uphold family ties, bear burdens, help the poor, honor guests, and support the truth."

  • Consulting Waraqah bin Naufal: She accompanied the Prophet to her cousin Waraqah bin Naufal, who confirmed that the angel was the great Namus (Gabriel) sent to Moses.

  • Enduring the Boycott: During the three agonizing years of economic and social boycott in the Ravine of Abu Talib, she spent her immense wealth to sustain the beleaguered Muslims.

Passing & Historical Legacy

Sayyidah Khadijah passed away in Mecca in 619 CE, shortly before the Hijrah, causing such profound grief that the year was designated 'Am al-Huzn (Year of Sorrow). The Prophet ﷺ cherished her memory for the remainder of his life, remembering her as the steadfast woman who believed when people disbelieved, and gave when people withheld.

Waraqah bin Naufal.meta:
Cousin of Khadijah
Era/Setting: Mecca, early 7th century CE
Waraqah bin Naufal.body:
Lineage & Early Life

Waraqah bin Naufal bin Asad bin Abdul Uzza was the paternal cousin of Sayyidah Khadijah. Before Islam, he rejected idol worship, maintained the monotheistic Abrahamic faith (Hanif), and embraced Christianity, becoming an accomplished scholar who translated biblical and sacred texts into Arabic and Hebrew.

Key Events & Historical Role

1. Monotheism in Pre-Islamic Mecca

  • Rejection of Idolatry: Along with figures like Zayd ibn Amr ibn Nufayl, Waraqah refused to participate in pagan sacrifices or bow before the stone idols of Quraysh.

2. Confirmation of Prophethood

  • Consultation with the Prophet ﷺ: When Sayyidah Khadijah brought young Muhammad to Waraqah after the terrifying encounter in Cave Hira, Waraqah listened attentively to the account of the revelation.

  • The Great Namus: Waraqah declared: "This is the Namus (Archangel Gabriel) that Allah sent down upon Moses. Would that I were a young man! Would that I might live to see the day when your people drive you out!"

  • Pledge of Support: When the Prophet inquired whether his own tribe would expel him, Waraqah affirmed that no messenger brought what he brought without facing hostility, pledging his staunch support if he lived to that day.

Passing & Historical Legacy

Waraqah passed away shortly thereafter during the period of cessation of revelation (Fatra). In authenticated narrations (Sahih Muslim and Sunan al-Tirmidhi), the Prophet ﷺ confirmed that he saw Waraqah in a dream clothed in white or walking in gardens of Paradise due to his early affirmation of truth.

Abu Bakar Asshiddiq.meta:
Birth name: Abdullah bin Abi Quhafah
Title: Ash-Shiddiq, Al-Atiq
Era/Setting: Mecca and Medina, 7th century CE
Abu Bakar Asshiddiq.body:
Lineage & Early Life

Abdullah bin Abi Quhafah (Abu Bakar Asshiddiq) hailed from the Banu Taym clan of Quraysh. Renowned throughout Mecca for his noble lineage, encyclopedic knowledge of Arab genealogy, immaculate morals, and successful commercial trading, he abstained from alcohol and pagan worship even in the pre-Islamic era.

Key Events & Historical Role

1. First Adult Male to Accept Islam

  • Unhesitating Faith: As the intimate childhood friend of Muhammad ﷺ, Abu Bakar accepted Islam immediately without a trace of hesitation when invited, earning the title Asshiddiq (The Truthful Witness).

  • Freeing the Oppressed: Using his vast wealth, he purchased and liberated tortured Muslim slaves in Mecca, including Bilal bin Rabah and Amir bin Fuhayrah.

2. Companion of the Cave & The Hijrah

  • Thani Ithnayn: Handpicked by the Prophet ﷺ to be his sole companion on the perilous migration (Hijrah) to Medina, sheltered in Cave Thawr where the Quran immortalized his devotion: "When they were in the cave, he said to his companion: Do not grieve; indeed Allah is with us" (At-Tawbah: 40).

3. The First Rightly-Guided Caliph (632–634 CE)

  • Steadfastness at the Prophet's Passing: Calmed the grief-stricken community with his legendary address: "Whoever worshipped Muhammad, Muhammad has passed; but whoever worships Allah, Allah is alive and never dies."

  • Unification & Riddah Wars: Dispatched Usama's expedition, defeated rebel apostates and false prophets, unified Arabia, and commissioned the landmark first compilation of the Holy Quran into a single codex (Mushaf).

Passing & Historical Legacy

Abu Bakar passed away in Medina in 634 CE (13 AH) and was laid to rest beside the Holy Prophet Muhammad ﷺ in the Prophet's Chamber. He is venerated as the greatest human being after the Prophets and Messengers.
